messages:
maya: Heads-up: kicking off a replay pass over last week's prod traces to validate anonymization + determinism across kernel choices and KV cache states. cc kevin, ryan :eyes:
perf-bot: Started replay job id=58342 (pinned kernel run) and job id=58343 (auto kernel run) on node-group=g4dn.xlarge.
kevin: Which sampling rate are we using? want to avoid bias toward short prompts that dominate prod.
maya: Using stratified sampling by prompt_length buckets: 0-64, 65-256, 256+. Weights = 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2. Anonymization: token-hash with salt per-customer. Config snippet:```json
{
  "sampling": {"buckets": [[0,64],[65,256],[257,9999]], "weights": [0.5,0.3,0.2]},
  "anonymize": true,
  "anonymize_mode": "token_hash",
  "seed": 12345
}
```
ryan: Good. We should also simulate both cold and warm KV cache. last time we saw parity diffs only when cache was cold and using quantized kernels.
maya: Plan: run cold (start with empty kv cache) and warm (seed by replaying the previous N requests in-trace to prefill kv cache). We'll compare: token-by-token parity, median/p95 latency, and kernel selection logs.
sophie: For determinism, run with --fixed-seed and disable async batching (set batching.mode=sync) so ordering is stable. Also pin kernel selection for the A run (e.g. opt-atten-v2) and allow auto selection for B.
kevin: Also bind to the same instance type + CUDA driver version so apples-to-apples. add hardware_affinity: g4dn.xlarge,cuda12.2
maya: Agreed. Canary jobs: 58342 = pinned kernel opt-atten-v2 (warm), 58343 = kernel auto (warm). I'll run cold runs next.
perf-bot: Job 58342 finished. metrics summary: median_latency=28ms, p95=112ms, throughput=420 req/s. parity_failures=12 out of 1000 sampled requests (1.2%).
ryan: Parity fail snippet (token diffs):```
--- expected tokens
+++ actual tokens
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 token_1023 token_1024 token_1025
-\u003cMASKED\u003e
+\u003cMASKED_ALT\u003e

Log excerpt: softmax logits diverged by ~2e-3 after quantized matmul when prefix_len > 256
```
maya: Looks like diffs cluster when sequence length > 256 and kv offset wrapping happens during cached attention. Hypothesis: quantized kernel path uses a slightly different accumulation order causing fp rounding to cross selection threshold.
kevin: Next steps: 1) deterministic repro with a small trace slice 2) re-run with higher-precision matmul (fp16->fp32) 3) attach per-op profiler and kernel selection trace.
maya: I'll run the deterministic repro now and capture per-op profiles (nvprof/trace) and the kernel selection log. Also verified anonymization: replaced PII with stable hashed tokens; parity still occurs so PII masking isn't the cause.
sophie: If we can reproduce deterministically, file an eng-runtime issue with the minimal trace + profiler. tag @eng-runtime and include job ids + slice path.
maya: Saved the failing slice at /replays/58342/slices/22 and uploaded profiler to s3://redwood-replays/58342/profiles/trace22.nvprof. Closing this thread once repro confirmed or blocked. Thanks!
